title: Parameter lifecycle: JSON definition format, runtime validation, and humanized error surfaces
creator: Aisha Patel
description: We need a compact, versioned JSON parameter definition format and a runtime validation strategy that balances developer ergonomics with production safety. Current tool-calling parameter handling is ad-hoc across SDKs and runtimes: some clients see cryptic validation failures, others silently coerce values leading to downstream errors. This ticket defines the spec, compatibility rules, human-friendly error codes, and rollout plan so teams can adopt safely and SDKs can surface actionable remediation steps.
background: Several customer bug reports and internal postmortems show two recurring issues: (1) opaque validation errors returned by the runtime that are hard for engineers to map back to a parameter mistake, and (2) breaking changes introduced by minor schema edits in model tool manifests. We have many related tickets exploring schema evolution and error UX, but lack a single, pragmatic format + runtime behavior that is easy to implement across hosted/dedicated/private deployments.
proposed_solution: Design a lightweight parameter manifest (v1) in JSON that supports: explicit field types (string, integer, float, enum, array, object-lite), optional/required semantics, examples, deprecation metadata, and a 'compatibility' mode flag. Runtime validation will implement three modes: strict (reject on violation), repair (attempt safe coercions with telemetry), and permissive (log-only). Errors will be normalized into an error envelope with stable error codes, human message, suggested remediation, and an example-correct payload. Provide SDK helper utilities for validation, client-side linting, and automated migration reports. Add telemetry hooks: validation.reason, validation.mode, manifest.version, and a sampling flag for anonymized payloads. Rollout via: (1) spec PR + design doc; (2) runtime implementation behind feature flag; (3) SDK adapters across JS/Python/Go; (4) Console UI to show schema diffs and recent validation errors per route.
tradeoffs: Keeping the manifest small avoids adoption friction but limits expressivity for deeply nested objects. We deliberately avoid full JSON Schema to keep runtime cost and cognitive load low. Three validation modes increase complexity in telemetry interpretation. Strict mode protects production but may cause customer breaks; repair mode reduces churn but risks masking application bugs. We'll mitigate with clear defaults (preserve existing permissive behavior for non-opt-in customers) and a strong migration UX.
acceptance_criteria: Spec doc merged to /docs/api/parameter-manifest-v1 with examples and compatibility rules
Runtime implements validation modes behind feature flag and passes performance regression tests (<5% p50 token latency impact in microbench)
JS/Python SDKs expose validator and generate actionable client errors matching envelope spec
Console shows per-route validation failures and schema diff view for 30-day window
Migration guide published and a small pilot with 2 customer teams completed

final_decision: Adopt compact manifest v1 with three runtime validation modes; default to permissive for non-opted-in routes. Enforce opt-in for sampling example payloads per legal guidance.
implementation_notes: Use a streaming-friendly validator that validates incremental fields as they arrive for streaming tool calls. Add a lightweight version tag in POST /tool-manifest headers to avoid model download thrash. Ensure validator code is sharable across hosted/dedicated/private by keeping no external dependencies and providing small, generated language bindings.
